races.title: Ban on data centers (initiated ordinance)
races.target_project: Project Milo (near Deer Creek Golf Course)
races.summary: Citizen-initiated ordinance prohibiting the construction of any data center within city limits, including converting existing buildings. No megawatt threshold: the only outright ban among Ohio's November measures. Council had already adopted a 12-month moratorium.
races.ballot_text: Shall the ordinance to approve or reject a ban on data centers within the city limits, be passed? (Ohio Secretary of State listing and Trumbull County BOE running list.) The ordinance defines a data center as "any facility that primarily contains electronic equipment used to process, store, and transmit digital information" and also bars converting an existing building into one (fragment per WKBN; full ordinance text not retrieved).
races.notes: Issue number not yet confirmed; check Trumbull BOE sample ballot. Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file.

races.title: Charter amendment banning data centers over 7.5 MW
races.target_project: Thor Equities proposal south of Rittal
races.proponents: Conserve Ohio / Nicole Nawman petition (400+ signatures)
races.summary: Adds Section 8.07 to Article VIII of the city charter prohibiting construction of data centers in the city, with an exemption for small privately owned facilities serving a single organization with peak demand under 7.5 MW. Council rescinded its data-center zoning allowance in June and adopted a 12-month moratorium; Thor Equities sued in federal court. A recall of the mayor is on the same ballot.
races.ballot_text: City of Urbana, Proposed Charter Amendment. A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article VIII of the Charter of the City of Urbana be amended to add Section 8.07, to read as follows? Article VIII, Section 8.07. Prohibition of a Data Center. (A) the construction of a data center is hereby prohibited. (B) as used in this Section, "construction" shall mean the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities and related activities, which include preparations and modifications for same, for a common purpose. (C) as used in this Section, "data center" shall mean one or more buildings or physical facilities or infrastructure, located on a single real property parcel or on contiguous, adjacent, or otherwise aggregated real property parcels that are used primarily or exclusively for digital information services such as the management, storage, processing and dissemination of electronic data and information, including but not limited to the implementation of artificial intelligence, through the use of computer systems, servers, networking equipment, and related components, including equipment cooling systems, or virtual currency mining. (D) this Section shall not apply to data centers, as defined in this section, whose sole purpose is to serve as a dedicated facility that supports the computing needs of a single organization or enterprise not otherwise engaged in the business of management, storage, processing, and/or dissemination of electronic data and information and which is wholly owned by that enterprise, and which has an aggregate monthly demand or peak load of less than seven-point-five (7.5) megawatts, however derived from any energy source, or a combination thereof. (E) this Section is self-executing. YES / NO
races.notes: Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Charter Amendment: Article VII, Section 8.07 (the petition's Article VII/VIII inconsistency carries through to the state list). Full text from the Champaign County sample ballot (Urbana 3-A), which prints it without an issue number; the ballot reads Article VIII.

races.title: Charter amendment banning data centers over 25 MW
races.target_project: Amazon Data Services campus (~$2B) in the city technology park
races.summary: Adds Article XI, Section 11.05 to the city charter prohibiting construction of data centers with aggregate monthly demand or peak electrical load over 25 MW. Self-executing. Council enacted a moratorium through Jan 31, 2027 while the vote is pending.
races.ballot_text: Proposed Charter Amendment, City of Sunbury. A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. The proposed amendment would amend the Charter of the City of Sunbury to add Section 11.05 to Article XI to read as follows: Article XI, Section 11.05: Prohibition of Construction of a Data Center. (A) The construction of a data center is hereby prohibited. (B) As used in this Section, "construction" shall mean the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities, and related activities, which include preparations and modifications for same, for a common purpose. (C) As used in this Section, "data center" shall mean one or more buildings or physical facilities or infrastructure, located on a single real property parcel or on contiguous, adjacent, or otherwise aggregated real property parcels that: (1) Are used primarily or exclusively for digital information services such as the management, storage, processing, and dissemination of electronic data and information through the use of computer systems, servers, networking equipment, and related components, including equipment cooling systems; and (2) Has an aggregate monthly demand or peak load of greater than twenty-five (25) megawatts, however derived from any energy source, or a combination thereof. (D) This Section is self-executing. Shall Article XI, Section 11.05 of the Charter of the City of Sunbury be adopted? YES / NO
races.notes: Delaware County Issue 9 is a different Sunbury charter amendment (council seats); confirm this measure's issue number. Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file (misspelled Sunsbury) as Charter Amendment: Article XI, Section XI. Full text from the Delaware County sample ballot (Sunbury City A), printed without an issue number.

races.title: Charter amendment banning data centers over 25 MW
races.target_project: No formal proposal (M2 Development feasibility study at Conneaut East Industrial Park)
races.opponents: City Manager Nick Sanford warned of judicial review
races.summary: Adds Article XVI, Conservation of Natural Resources, to the city charter, prohibiting data centers with aggregate monthly demand or peak load over 25 MW (318 valid signatures). Council declined to adopt a moratorium; the petition went forward anyway.
races.ballot_text: Charter amendment adding Article XVI, "Conservation of Natural Resources," prohibiting data centers with an aggregate demand or peak load above 25 megawatts, with the 25 MW definition aggregated across parcels and counted from any energy source or combination (summary per the Star Beacon and OpenVoterGuide; the ballot text itself was not retrieved).
races.notes: NOT present in the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3 Local Questions and Issues file (the only Ashtabula County Conneaut row is a park district levy); the measure is confirmed by the Ashtabula County BOE's Aug 26 approval and News 5 Cleveland. Verify with the county sample ballot.

races.title: Charter amendment banning data centers over 25 MW
races.summary: Adds Section 1.12 to the city charter prohibiting construction of data centers with a monthly or peak load greater than 25 MW. First petition-driven charter amendment since the 1983 charter; council also adopted a six-month moratorium.
races.ballot_text: Charter amendment adding Section 1.12 to Article I: (A) "the construction of a data center is hereby prohibited"; (B) "construction" means "the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities, and related activities, which include preparations and modifications for same, for a common purpose"; (C) "data center" "shall mean one or more buildings or physical facilities or infrastructure" on one parcel or aggregated adjacent parcels, used primarily for digital information services, with peak load or aggregated monthly demand above 25 megawatts regardless of how the power is generated; self-executing. (Quoted fragments verbatim per the Crescent-News; the ballot question line was not retrieved.)
races.notes: Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Charter Amendment: Section 1.12.

races.title: Charter amendment banning data centers over 25 MW
races.target_project: Proposed ~600-acre Amazon campus (Madison/St. Clair townships); existing AWS site unaffected
races.summary: Adds Article IX, Section 9.06 to the charter: data center construction is prohibited where aggregate monthly demand or peak load exceeds 25 MW from any energy source or combination; self-executing. Council refused to certify the petition until the Ohio Supreme Court ordered it onto the ballot (State ex rel. Blankenship v. Trenton City Council, 2026-Ohio-3406). Council has teed up a property-tax holiday contingent on the measure failing, and litigation is expected if it passes.
races.ballot_text: Proposed Charter Amendment. A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Article IX, Section 9.06, Prohibition of Construction of a Data Center: (A) "The construction of a data center is hereby prohibited." (B) "As used in this Section, 'construction' shall mean the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities, and related activities [...]" (C) a data center is one or more buildings, physical facilities or infrastructure on a single parcel "or on contiguous, adjacent, or otherwise aggregated real property parcels" that is used primarily for digital information services and "(2) Has an aggregate monthly demand or peak load of greater than twenty five (25) megawatts" from any energy source or combination. (D) "This Section is self-executing." (Per WVXU and the Journal-News reproducing the Butler County ballot text; the "Shall Article IX..." question line was not captured.)
races.notes: Ohio Supreme Court ordered the measure onto the ballot Sept 1, 2026. Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Charter Amendment: Article IX, Section 9.06.

races.title: Community Consent Amendment (voter approval for large developments)
races.target_project: ~300-acre data center proposal (Beatty/Rensch Rd)
races.summary: Creates a mandatory public referendum for any development of 50 or more acres, more than 20 MW peak demand, or more than 500,000 gallons of water per day, with the developer paying election costs. Not a ban, but it would subject the proposed data center to a citywide vote. City moratorium runs through June 2027.
races.ballot_text: Issue 28, Community Consent Amendment: creates a public referendum process for large developments (Franklin County Board of Elections certified description). Per the city's Issue 28 page, a public vote would be required before the city approves a development that occupies 50 or more contiguous acres, uses more than 20 megawatts of electricity at peak capacity, or uses more than 500,000 gallons of water per day, and for expansions of existing properties that increase acreage, power demand or water use by 10 percent or more. (The full amendment text is in the county's Issue 28 PDF; the ballot question line was not retrieved.)
races.notes: Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Charter Amendment: XI. The county link named Grove-City-Charter-Amendment-5 serves a 2017 notice of election, not Issue 28; the Issue 28 full-text PDF is a separate link on vote.franklincountyohio.gov/election-info/2026.

races.title: Charter amendment banning data centers over 25 MW
races.target_project: Aligned Data Centers 200 MW, three-building site plan (rejected by council 7-0)
races.proponents: Citizen petition (500+ signatures, Conserve Ohio language)
races.summary: Adds Section 11.09 to the charter prohibiting construction of a data center within city limits, using the 25 MW monthly-demand definition. One of four Pataskala charter amendments on the ballot. Aligned is seeking judicial review of the council's rejection.
races.ballot_text: CITY OF PATASKALA Charter Amendment. Shall Section 11.09 (Prohibitation of a Data Center) be added therby prohibiting the constuction of a data center within the City limits? (Verbatim from the Licking County Board of Elections filed-issues list, typos included. The section defines a data center as facilities used primarily or exclusively for digital information services with aggregate monthly demand or peak load greater than 25 megawatts, aggregated across contiguous parcels.)
races.notes: The Licking County BOE summary shows no megawatt threshold; news reports describe the 25 MW definition. One of four Pataskala charter amendments plus a library levy on the same ballot. Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Charter Amendment: Article XI, Section 11.09 (three other Pataskala charter amendments are on the same ballot). Question confirmed against the Licking County issues list (8 precincts).

races.title: Charter amendment prohibiting data centers (Section 10.12)
races.target_project: None proposed (largely symbolic)
races.summary: Adds Section 10.12 (Prohibition of a Data Center) to the village charter with the 25 MW definition. No project is proposed in Granville.
races.ballot_text: VILLAGE OF GRANVILLE Charter Amendment. Shall Section 10.12 (Prohibitation of a Data Center) be added therby prohibiting the constuction of a data center within the City limits? (Verbatim from the Licking County Board of Elections filed-issues list, typos and City limits included; three Granville precincts. The section uses the 25 MW definition.)
races.notes: Some roundups describe it as an outright ban; confirm threshold in the certified text. Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Charter Amendment: Article X, Section 10.12.

races.title: Charter amendment capping data centers at 25 MW
races.target_project: Proposed data center on farmland in Oregon
races.summary: Writes a 25 MW cap into the city charter using the Conserve Ohio template. Organizers frame it as steering development to brownfield and industrial sites.
races.ballot_text: Issue 25. Shall the Charter of the City of Oregon be amended to add Section 8 to Article XIII to read as follows? Article XIII, Section 8; Prohibition of Construction of a Data Center. (A) The construction of a data center is hereby prohibited. (B) As used in this Section, "construction" shall mean the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities, and related activities, which include preparations and modifications for the same, for a common purpose. (C) As used in this Section, "data center" shall mean one or more buildings or physical facilities or infrastructure, located on a single property parcel or on contiguous, adjacent, or otherwise aggregated real property parcels that: (1) Are used primarily or exclusively for digital information services such as the management, storage, processing, and dissemination of electronic data and information through the use of computing systems, servers, networking equipment, and related components, including equipment cooling systems; and (2) Has an aggregate monthly demand or peak load of greater than twenty-five (25) megawatts, however derived from any energy source, or combination thereof. (D) This section is self-executing. Per the city: a YES vote is in support of the charter change and prohibition of data centers greater than 25 MW; a NO vote is in opposition.
races.notes: Issue 25 (Issues 26 and 27 on the Oregon ballot are unrelated charter changes). Council accepted the BOE certification Aug 19. Lucas County reports on the SOS-hosted ENR platform (Nov 2025 was instance 21). Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Charter Amendment: Article XIII, Section 8. Full text from the city's 2026 Election for Voters page.

races.title: Proposed ordinance allowing data center development
races.target_project: Decimal Digital AI data center pitch
races.summary: A proposed village ordinance that would allow data center development within village limits, put to voters as an adopt-or-reject question. Earlier reporting described it as advisory; the Secretary of State's list shows a binding proposed ordinance. The village adopted a 12-month moratorium in February after Decimal Digital's pitch and is still owed about $1.3M from a 2024 crypto-mining operation.
races.ballot_text: Shall the proposed ordinance allowing data center development be adopted?
races.notes: A YES vote favors allowing data centers. Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Village of Monroeville: Shall the proposed ordinance allowing data center development be adopted? Who placed it (council or petition) is unverified.

races.summary: Township zoning adoption under ORC Chapter 519, which requires voter approval. Adopting zoning gives the township authority over the proposed data center at the former Stuart power plant; trustees passed a one-year voluntary moratorium in March.
races.ballot_text: Initiative establishing zoning regulations for the unincorporated area of Sprigg Township (ORC Chapter 519 zoning adoption; the Ohio Capital Journal describes the plan as meant to preserve the township's rural and agricultural character in response to a potential data center). Ballot wording not yet retrieved.
races.notes: Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Sprigg Township, Zoning amendment.

races.title: Referendum on Resolution 06-2026 (EdgeConneX development agreement)
races.target_project: EdgeConneX: two data centers and a gas plant on ~195 acres
races.proponents: Teays Valley Community Alliance (petition, 669 valid signatures)
races.summary: Referendum on the council's April resolution approving a development and supply agreement term summary with EdgeConneX. The Ohio Supreme Court ordered the petition certified (State ex rel. McNamara-Smith v. Grube, 2026-Ohio-3035). A YES vote upholds the agreement; a NO vote rejects it (though it does not by itself stop construction). EdgeConneX paid the village $3.5M in October.
races.ballot_text: Referendum (By Petition), Village of Ashville: Shall the resolution enacting approval of a development and supply agreement term summary with EdgeConneX be approved? Voting YES is voting FOR Resolution 06-2026; voting NO is voting AGAINST it. (Question as quoted from the Pickaway County ballot proofs by the Circleville Herald and Scioto Post.)
races.notes: A YES vote is the pro-data-center side. Council's attempt to repeal the agreement (Resolution 16-2026) failed at its third reading on Oct 5, 2026, so the referendum stays on the ballot. Village electors only. Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file with the same question wording.

races.title: Ban on high-impact data centers in all zoning districts
races.target_project: Proposed data center bid (~$3M, funding source contested in court)
races.opponents: Regional Development Association of East Central Kansas; city staff
races.summary: Citizen-initiated ordinance (K.S.A. 12-3013) prohibiting the construction, installation, operation and maintenance of High Impact Data Centers in every zoning district. A High Impact Data Center is one with peak electrical load over 10 MW or daily water draw over 100,000 gallons, including server farms, colocation, AI training and crypto mining. A district court ordered the question onto the ballot; the city's declaratory-judgment case on whether the subject is a proper initiative is still pending, so if approved the ordinance takes effect only after a ruling. Companion Question #3 would ban large battery storage.
races.ballot_text: Explanatory Statement: This ordinance would prohibit the construction, installation, operation, and maintenance of High Impact Data Centers within the City of Emporia, Kansas. A "High Impact Data Center" is defined as a facility whose primary purpose is the housing, operation, and maintenance of computer servers and related infrastructure that requires a peak electrical load exceeding ten (10) megawatts or a daily water draw exceeding one hundred thousand (100,000) gallons. This term includes server farms, colocation facilities, AI training facilities, cryptocurrency mining operations, and similar high-density computing facilities. The prohibition would apply to all zoning districts within the City. [...] Shall the following ordinance be adopted? An Ordinance of the City of Emporia, Kansas prohibiting the installation and operation of High Impact Data Centers to protect the health, safety and welfare of the residents of Emporia, Kansas. (Verbatim fragments from the city ballot-information page; the ordinance's operative sections as printed were not retrieved.)
races.notes: Polls close 7 pm Central. Local Question No. 2; Question No. 3 is the companion battery-storage ban. A YES vote adopts the ordinance. The Emporia Gazette reports the petition text cites a nonexistent code article; the city's judicial-review case on whether the subject is a proper initiative is pending, so if approved the ordinance cannot take effect until that is resolved.

races.title: Ten-year ban on high-impact data centers and large battery storage
races.target_project: Possible data center project discussed in April 2026
races.opponents: City of El Dorado (lost court challenge)
races.summary: Citizen-initiated ordinance prohibiting High Impact Data Centers and Tier 2 and Tier 3 battery energy storage systems. Under K.S.A. 12-3013, if adopted by voters it cannot be amended or repealed by the commission for ten years without voter approval. The Butler County District Court ruled the petition a proper legislative subject; the commission placed it on the ballot 5-0 on Aug 25.
races.ballot_text: Shall the following ordinance be adopted? [ordinance title] prohibiting the installation and operation of High Impact Data Centers and Tier 2 and Tier 3 Battery Energy Storage Systems. Per the city, the question as printed carries the ordinance title, the definitions (a high impact data center has a peak electrical load exceeding 10 megawatts or a daily water draw exceeding 100,000 gallons; Tier 2 storage has aggregate capacity between 81 and 600 kilowatt-hours or more than one storage technology in a room or enclosed area; Tier 3 exceeds 600 kilowatt-hours) and a statement that the ordinance remains in effect for ten years unless amended or repealed by voter approval of a ballot question. (Reconstructed from city notices 652 and 688 and news coverage; the certified question text was not retrieved.)
races.notes: Polls close 7 pm Central. Results page URL unverified. Butler County District Court ruled in August that the ordinance is legislative and may proceed by initiative (city notice 683).

races.title: Ban on data centers over 25 MW
races.target_project: Lightfield Energy Proximity Park (~300 acres, contract since terminated)
races.opponents: City of Ottawa (outside counsel called the ordinance administrative)
races.summary: Citizen-initiated ordinance prohibiting data centers that use more than 25 MW within city limits. Judge Eric Godderz ordered the question onto the ballot; a hearing on Oct 20, 2026 will decide whether the ordinance is legislative or administrative, which determines whether a YES vote takes effect. The city has since terminated the Lightfield sales contract.
races.ballot_text: Citizen-initiated ordinance barring the city from allowing or constructing any data center using more than 25 megawatts of power within city limits. Per KSHB and KOFO: a YES vote would restrict any data center built in Ottawa to no more than 25 megawatts; a NO vote would allow construction of data centers that use more than 25 megawatts. (Paraphrase; the certified question text was not retrieved.)
races.notes: Polls close 7 pm Central. Court hearing Oct 20, 2026.

races.notes: A YES vote favors data centers. Wording reproduced verbatim in the Alton Telegraph voter guide; the other three townships use the identical form.

races.title: Advisory: restrictions on data centers countywide
races.target_project: CyrusOne ~$500M data center near Waverly (approved by neighboring Sangamon County)
races.proponents: Accountability for Data Center Development; Indivisible Jacksonville (1,100+ signatures)
races.summary: Non-binding countywide question. Morgan County has no zoning and a six-month moratorium on data center applications; commissioners say they lack power to deny projects without zoning.
races.ballot_text: Shall there be restrictions imposed on the construction and operation of data centers in Morgan County? (Wording per WLDS's October report; the petition-stage draft read: Should there be restrictions imposed on the construction of data centers in Morgan County? The certified ballot was not retrieved.)
races.notes: WLDS reported two wordings (Shall there be restrictions imposed on the construction and operation of data centers / Should there be restrictions imposed on the construction of data centers); confirm against the certified ballot. Results post on the GBS portal (results.gbsvote.com). Polls close 7 pm Central.

races.title: Voter approval required for projects over $450M at the GM/JATCO site
races.target_project: Viridian Partners' proposed 800 MW, ~$8B data center campus on the former GM site (letter of intent lapsed)
races.summary: Direct legislation under Wis. Stat. 9.20 requiring that development agreements, projects, sales and leases at the city-owned GM/JATCO sites (1000 General Motors Dr. and 544 Kellogg Ave. plus adjacent parcels in the same development) involving more than $450 million in project costs be approved by a majority of Janesville electors; phased projects aggregate toward the threshold. The question does not mention data centers but was written to stop the Viridian campus; the city also has a separate data center moratorium.
races.ballot_text: Should approval of development agreements, development projects, sales, and leases at the GM/JATCO sites for projects over $450 million be decided by a majority vote of the electors? (Reconstructed from verbatim fragments reported by WMTV, the Gazette and the Badger Institute; the full sentence as printed was not retrieved. The ordinance covers 1000 General Motors Drive and 544 Kellogg Ave. plus adjacent properties in the same development, treats phased developments as one project, and does not use the words data center.)
races.notes: Polls close 8 pm Central. Janesville absentee ballots are counted centrally and reported separately.

races.title: Voter-locked ban on data centers in all zones
races.target_project: Pre-emptive; follows neighboring Monterey Park
races.summary: Affirms the council's existing zoning ban on data centers by voter action, so a future council cannot repeal it without going back to voters. Simple majority.
races.ballot_text: Data Centers Prohibited. Shall an ordinance be adopted affirming the Council adopted ban on "Data Centers" by amending the Alhambra Municipal Code to again define "Data Centers" and prohibit them in all zones of the City?
races.notes: Polls close 8 pm Pacific. LA County JSON feed: results.lavote.gov/electionresults/json?electionid=ID (June 2, 2026 primary was 4338; the Nov 3 id appears when the election is listed).

races.title: Allow data centers in the Eldorado Valley Transfer Area
races.target_project: Roughly 14,000 acres of city-owned desert outside the tortoise habitat easement
races.summary: City Charter section 144(1) requires voter approval of any new permitted use in the Eldorado Valley Transfer Area. A YES vote makes data centers an approved land use on the roughly 14,000 acres outside the habitat conservation easement; individual leases would still need the Land Management Plan process and council approval.
races.ballot_text: Should data center facilities be an approved land use within the Eldorado Valley Transfer Area outside of the Multi-species Habitat Conservation Easement? City explanation: if passed, the City Council would only be authorized to potentially enter into leases allowing data center facilities; any proposed project would still require further city review. If it fails, no data center facilities would be approved within the Eldorado Valley Transfer Area outside of the Multi-species Habitat Conservation Easement.
races.notes: A YES vote is the pro-data-center side. Polls close 7 pm Pacific. Wording per the city Explanation and Digest and Nevada Current. The 2024 NV SOS Clark County page listed Boulder City questions, so the SOS page should carry this one too.

races.title: Prohibit New Data Centers charter amendment
races.target_project: Pre-emptive (no project pending)
races.summary: Charter amendment prohibiting the permitting, construction, expansion or operation of new data centers within city limits, covering cloud, AI, crypto-mining and colocation facilities. Council enacted an ordinance ban in September to prevent an approval before the vote; proponents argue a charter provision is more durable because a future council could repeal an ordinance.
races.ballot_text: Charter amendment that would "prohibit the approval, construction, expansion, or operation of new data centers within the city" (phrase quoted from the ordinance at first reading, per ClickOrlando) and bar the city from issuing development approvals or permits for such facilities. The official ballot title and summary have not been retrieved; the "Charter Amendment 4" label comes from local coverage rather than an official source.
races.notes: Polls close 7 pm Eastern (Volusia is in the Eastern zone). The amendment is one of seven charter questions the council sent to the ballot Aug 3, 2026. Confirm the official number and summary on the Volusia County sample ballot.

races.title: Prohibit data centers citywide (General Plan amendment)
races.target_project: Proposed ~250,000 sq ft, up-to-50 MW data center on a former mall site
races.summary: Amends the General Plan land-use element to prohibit data centers citywide; changeable only by a future public vote. Widely described as the first voter-approved permanent data center ban in the country.
races.ballot_text: Community Act Prohibiting Data Centers. Shall the ordinance amending the City of Monterey Park General Plan to prohibit data centers citywide to protect air quality, drinking water resources and public health... (opening of the question per Resolution No. 2026-R6; the remainder, which references electricity and water rates and keeps the prohibition in place until voters end it, was not captured verbatim)
races.result_note: Passed 88.3% yes (10,321 to 1,362), certified LA County results as reported by secondary sources.
races.notes: Placement (citizen vs council) unconfirmed.

races.title: Voter approval required for large tax incremental districts
races.target_project: Vantage Data Centers / OpenAI-Oracle Stargate campus and the $458M TID No. 5
races.opponents: Metropolitan Milwaukee Association of Commerce and others (lawsuit pending)
races.summary: Bars the city from creating or approving a tax incremental district with a projected base value of $10 million or more, or project costs over $10 million, without voter approval. Prospective only; does not affect the Vantage campus already under construction.
races.ballot_text: Shall the City of Port Washington adopt the proposed ordinance, which, if adopted, would bar the City from creating or approving a Tax Incremental District that requires a large capital expenditure, or with a base value projected to or exceeding $10,000,000.00, or project costs exceeding $10,000,000.00 [...] (remainder, per coverage: unless approved by city electors at a referendum; verbatim excerpt per WTMJ's voter guide, cut off in the source)
races.result_note: Passed 66.4% yes (2,710 to 1,371), unofficial Ozaukee County count.
races.notes: Called the nation's first anti-data-center referendum. Lawsuit pending.

races.title: Advisory: support utility infrastructure for a large data center?
races.target_project: Cloverleaf Infrastructure land scouting
races.summary: Non-binding question on whether the village should authorize, support, participate in or facilitate municipal utility infrastructure tied to a large-scale data center. Voters rejected it overwhelmingly; the village had already adopted a one-year moratorium.
races.ballot_text: Advisory question, beginning with Should, asking whether the Village should authorize, support, participate in or facilitate municipal utility infrastructure and related improvements tied to a large-scale data center development within or affecting the Village. (Paraphrase assembled from NBC26, Spectrum News and WBAY; no verbatim text surfaced.)
races.result_note: Failed: 87.2% no (1,033 to 151). A NO vote was the anti-data-center outcome.

races.measure_label: General Industrial Zoning Ordinance Ballot Proposal
races.title: Referendum on rezoning 522 acres for a data center campus
races.target_project: Thor Equities (Form8tion) ~$1B data center campus
races.summary: Zoning referendum under the Michigan Zoning Enabling Act on Ordinance 2025-02, which rezoned seven parcels (522 acres) from agricultural residential to general industrial. A YES vote would have upheld the rezoning; voters repealed it by nearly nine to one.
races.ballot_text: General Industrial Zoning Ordinance Ballot Proposal. Shall the Charter Township of Augusta adopt Ordinance No. 2025-02 to amend the [zoning ordinance and zoning map so that the Augusta Development Corp. properties] (T-20-32-200-010, T-20-32-100-008, T-20-32-400-001, T-20-32-400-012, T-20-32-400-013, T-20-32-300-014, T-20-32-300-013) be rezoned from AR, Agricultural Residential to GI, General Industrial? (Head and tail verbatim from the Washtenaw County official list of proposals; bracketed middle reconstructed from the township resolution.)
races.result_note: Rezoning repealed: 89.6% no (2,314 to 269), 2 of 2 precincts.

races.title: Should elected officials allow data centers in Bulloch County?
races.target_project: Proposed data centers in Bulloch County
races.summary: Non-binding party question on the Republican primary ballot.
races.ballot_text: Should elected officials allow the building of data centers in Bulloch County?
races.result_note: About 76% of Republican primary voters voted no (per a county commissioner; official tally not retrieved).

races.title: Should data centers be built in Bulloch County?
races.target_project: Proposed data centers in Bulloch County
races.summary: Non-binding party question on the Democratic primary ballot.
races.ballot_text: Should data centers be built in Bulloch County?
races.result_note: About 78% of Democratic primary voters voted no (per a county commissioner; official tally not retrieved).

races.title: Support data centers if they significantly lower property taxes?
races.summary: Non-binding party question.
races.ballot_text: If bringing Data Centers to Glynn County would significantly lower your property taxes, would you be for data centers?
races.result_note: Result not yet retrieved (in the county's May 19 summary report).

races.title: Require hearings and environmental studies for data centers?
races.summary: Non-binding party question.
races.ballot_text: Should DeKalb County require public hearings and strict environmental impact studies for all new potential data center developments?
races.result_note: Passed overwhelmingly: about 94% for (138,696 to 8,177) per the Wikipedia summary of the party advisory election; confirm against the SOS county drill-down.

races.title: Require full disclosure before approving data centers?
races.summary: Non-binding party question.
races.ballot_text: Should Columbia County require full public disclosure of water use, power demand, tax incentives, and infrastructure impacts before approving any new data center development or large industrial development?

races.title: Should electric bills rise to support data center power usage?
races.summary: Non-binding party question.
races.ballot_text: Should your electric bill be increased to support data center power usage?
races.result_note: Result not yet retrieved (county official summary report).

races.title: Bond and noise guarantee for hyperscale data centers seeking tax breaks
races.target_project: Province Group proposal (village declined its abatement/PILOT request in July)
races.summary: Citizen-initiated ordinance requiring any hyperscale data center developer (over 10,000 sq ft, over 5,000 servers, or over 50 MW) that seeks a tax abatement, PILOT or other special tax designation to first deposit a bond or escrow equal to at least the projected tax revenue over the project's 31-year life plus projected salaries for 200 full-time employees, with annual make-whole payments if projections fall short and assessments for environmental, standard-of-living or property-value effects. Also requires a noise guarantee of 50 dB by day and 45 dB overnight with council-set fines. Conditions the deal rather than banning the building.
races.ballot_text: Shall the ordinance amending Chapter 133.01 "Established; Power & Duties" of the codified ordinances of the Village of Perry be adopted? (Ohio Secretary of State listing; Lake County Issue 16.) The ordinance requires hyperscale data center developers (over 10,000 square feet, 5,000 servers or 50 MW) seeking a tax abatement, PILOT or special tax designation to post a 31-year bond covering projected tax revenue and 200 salaries, with make-whole payments and a 50 dB day / 45 dB night noise guarantee.
races.notes: Found Oct 15 as the jurisdiction missing from the earlier list; with Piqua (moved to Feb 2027) it reconciles Ballotpedia's 21 measures / 18 jurisdictions. Confirmed as Issue 16 on the Lake County certified issues list.
